proceedings.outcome: refused to grant “humanitarian visas” to the applicants
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 13 September 2016 the Aliens Office, the administrative body responsible for issuing visas (see paragraph 45 below), refused to grant “humanitarian visas” to the applicants

proceedings.outcome: ordered a stay of execution of the refusals by the Aliens Office to grant visas and instructed the Belgian State to take new decisions within 48 hours
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 7 October 2016 the Aliens Appeals Board, acting under the extremely urgent procedure, ordered a stay of execution of the refusals by the Aliens Office to grant visas and instructed the Belgian State to take new decisions within 48 hours

proceedings.outcome: refusing to grant the visas
proceedings.supporting_quote: As required by the order of the Aliens Appeals Board (see paragraph 15 above), the Aliens Office issued new decisions, dated 10 October 2016, refusing to grant the visas

proceedings.outcome: ordered a stay of execution of the decision of 10 October 2016 refusing to issue the visas, and instructed the Aliens Office to take new decisions
proceedings.supporting_quote: By a judgment of 14 October 2016 the Aliens Appeals Board, acting under the extremely urgent procedure, again ordered a stay of execution of the decision of 10 October 2016 refusing to issue the visas, and instructed the Aliens Office to take new decisions

proceedings.outcome: refusing to issue the visas
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 17 October 2016 the Aliens Office again took decisions refusing to issue the visas, citing the same reasons as in the previous refusals.

proceedings.outcome: ordered a stay of execution of the refusal decisions of 17 October 2016 and directed the State to issue the applicants, within 48 hours, with laissez-passers or visas
proceedings.supporting_quote: By a judgment of 20 October 2016 the Aliens Appeals Board, essentially reiterating the substance of its previous judgments, ordered a stay of execution of the refusal decisions of 17 October 2016. In addition... it considered that it was justified to direct the State to issue the applicants, within 48 hours, with laissez-passers or visas, valid for three months.

proceedings.deciding_body: the President of the Brussels French-language Court of First Instance (“TPI”)
proceedings.outcome: ordered the State, as an urgent measure, to comply with the Board’s judgment of 20 October 2016... and made the order subject to a penalty payment
proceedings.supporting_quote: By an order of 25 October 2016... the acting president of the French-language TPI ordered the State, as an urgent measure, to comply with the Board’s judgment of 20 October 2016, that is, to issue the applicants with visas or laissez-passers , and made the order subject to a penalty payment of 1,000 euros (EUR) per day of delay and per applicant.

proceedings.deciding_body: the President of the French-language TPI
proceedings.outcome: declared their application admissible but unfounded
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 7 November 2016 another judge acting as president of the French ‑ language TPI declared their application admissible but unfounded

proceedings.outcome: ordered the Belgian State to execute the Aliens Appeals Board’s judgment of 20 October 2016... and ruled that the State was to pay a penalty of EUR 1,000 per day of delay and per applicant
proceedings.supporting_quote: In consequence, the court of appeal ordered the Belgian State to execute the Aliens Appeals Board’s judgment of 20 October 2016, which had instructed the Belgian authorities to issue visas or laissez-passers , held that this order was immediately enforceable and, lastly, ruled that the State was to pay a penalty of EUR 1,000 per day of delay and per applicant.

proceedings.deciding_body: the President of the Brussels Dutch-speaking TPI
proceedings.outcome: unsuccessful (request for stay of execution denied)
proceedings.supporting_quote: The Belgian State... lodged a unilateral action to that effect with the President of the Brussels Dutch ‑ speaking TPI on 13 December 2016, but was unsuccessful (order of the same date).

proceedings.outcome: varied the decision of the first-instance court... and ordered the applicants not to pursue further enforcement proceedings pending a decision by the enforcement judge
proceedings.supporting_quote: However, on an appeal by the Belgian State, the court of appeal varied the decision of the first-instance court in a judgment of 14 December 2016... and ordered the applicants not to pursue further enforcement proceedings pending a decision by the enforcement judge

proceedings.deciding_body: the enforcement judge at the Brussels French-language TPI
proceedings.outcome: proceedings brought to ensure payment order was executed (outcome not stated)
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 15 December 2016 the applicants brought an action against the Belgian State before the enforcement judge at the Brussels French-language TPI, seeking to ensure that the payment order of 13 December 2016 was executed.

proceedings.deciding_body: the enforcement judge at the Brussels Dutch-language TPI
proceedings.outcome: proceedings brought seeking stay of execution (outcome not stated)
proceedings.supporting_quote: On the same date the Belgian State brought proceedings against the applicants before the enforcement judge at the Brussels Dutch ‑ language TPI, seeking a stay of execution of the principal sentence

proceedings.outcome: dismissed the application to have those decisions set aside
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 24 March 2017 the Aliens Appeals Board dismissed the application to have those decisions set aside, finding that the Aliens Office’s decisions of 13 September 2016 (see paragraph 11 above) had become final

proceedings.outcome: dismissed the application to have the decisions set aside and ordered that the stay of execution in respect of the visa refusal decisions be lifted
proceedings.supporting_quote: By a judgment of 24 March 2017 the Aliens Appeals Board dismissed the application to have the decisions set aside and ordered that the stay of execution in respect of the visa refusal decisions be lifted

proceedings.outcome: decided in consequence to lift the stay of execution of the visa refusal decisions and the interim measures
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 6 March 2017 the Aliens Appeals Board noted that no application had been brought to have the decisions of 13 September 2016 refusing to issue the visas set aside, and decided in consequence to lift the stay of execution of the visa refusal decisions and the interim measures.

proceedings.outcome: held that the Aliens Appeals Boards’ judgment of 20 October 2016 was no longer operative... The court of appeal’s judgment of 7 December 2016 was thus no longer operative
proceedings.supporting_quote: By a judgment of 30 June 2017 a Dutch-language division of the Court of Appeal held that the Aliens Appeals Boards’ judgment of 20 October 2016 was no longer operative... The court of appeal’s judgment of 7 December 2016 was thus no longer operative

proceedings.outcome: dismissed an appeal on points of law by the applicants against the judgment of 6 March 2017
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 8 February 2018 the Conseil d’État dismissed an appeal on points of law by the applicants against the judgment of 6 March 2017.

proceedings.outcome: dismissed an appeal on points of law brought by the Belgian State against the judgment of 7 October 2016
proceedings.supporting_quote: On the same date the Conseil d’État dismissed an appeal on points of law brought by the Belgian State against the judgment of 7 October 2016

proceedings.instance_level: cassation (administrative appeal on points of law)
proceedings.outcome: dismissed [the appeal]
proceedings.supporting_quote: An administrative appeal on points of law lodged by the applicants against that judgment was dismissed by the Conseil d’État on 17 May 2018.

proceedings.outcome: dismissed [the appeal]
proceedings.supporting_quote: An appeal on points of law against this judgment was dismissed by the Conseil d’État in a judgment of 17 May 2018, on the same grounds as those set out in the above-cited judgment of the same date

proceedings.outcome: found that the case had become devoid of purpose
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 20 December 2017 the French-language enforcement judge, examining the action brought by the applicants on 15 December 2016, found that the case had become devoid of purpose following the Brussels Court of Appeal’s judgment of 30 June 2017.
